lessons.title: Pizza Hut: History & Brands
lessons.summary: Founders, landmark dates, brands and Gamma's role.

sections.heading: How it started
sections.body: Frank and Dan Carney founded Pizza Hut in Wichita, Kansas, USA.
keyPoints: 26 November 1993: first Sri Lankan Pizza Hut opened at Union Place
sections.memoryTip: Remember: 1958 worldwide → 1993 Sri Lanka.

sections.heading: Brands and franchise
sections.body: Yum! Brands includes KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and Habit Burger. Gamma Pizzakraft Lanka (Pvt) Ltd is the sole Sri Lankan franchisee for Pizza Hut and Taco Bell.
keyPoints: Yum! Brands is listed as the parent company
Gamma operates Pizza Hut and Taco Bell locally
sections.memoryTip: Remember the four brands and Gamma's two franchise brands.

lessons.title: Outlet Types: RBD, RR, DELCO & FCD
lessons.summary: Compare the four outlet formats named in the booklet.

sections.heading: RBD and Red Roof
sections.body: RBD (Restaurant Based Delivery) provides dine-in, carryout and delivery, with an emphasis on table service. Red Roof (RR) is described as similar to RBD but without delivery.
sections.memoryTip: Think: RBD delivers; RR does not.

sections.heading: DELCO and FCD
sections.body: DELCO stands for Delivery/Carryout; it sells approved products for carryout and delivery. FCD (Fast Casual Delco) includes dine-in, carryout and delivery, with counter ordering and an open-kitchen/fast-service format.
keyPoints: Jaffna was Sri Lanka's first FCD outlet
sections.memoryTip: DELCO = two channels; FCD = three with counter ordering.

lessons.title: Danger Zone, Fire & First Aid
lessons.summary: Key emergency visual mnemonics from the booklet.

sections.heading: Food danger zone
sections.body: The food danger zone is 5°C–65°C. Cold holding is below 5°C; hot holding is above 65°C.
keyPoints: Use updated approved outlet standards for live operations
sections.memoryTip: Remember: below 5°C or above 65°C. Follow current approved food-safety procedures.

sections.heading: Fire triangle
sections.body: The diagram identifies three elements required for a fire.
sections.memoryTip: Remove one element to stop the fire triangle.

sections.heading: PASS extinguisher method
sections.body: PASS — the four steps for extinguisher use.
keyPoints: A — Aim at the base of the fire
S — Sweep from side to side
sections.memoryTip: PASS = Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.

sections.heading: First-aid focus
sections.body: First aid focuses on the three Ps.
sections.memoryTip: Use local emergency-response procedures; the training content is an overview.
